extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for PR practitioners on when to use and how to draft press releases that announce newsworthy items and attract press coverage or target-audience attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are used to announce something that is newsworthy with the purpose of getting press coverage and getting noticed by your target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame a release around a clearly newsworthy announcement and keep the goal top-of-mind: earning press coverage and reaching a defined target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether a press release is necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand if a press release is actually needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the biggest mistakes brands make is thinking that every announcement or story deserves a press release. Communicators should ask themselves if the news is worthy of a press release, or if a pitch or social post will work better. Also consider whether a release is the best use of time and resources for this particular announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use distribution services appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Today distribution services like PR Newswire help brands get their news out to hundreds of publications in a matter of seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage established distribution services when broad, rapid dissemination is desired, but weigh their cost and fit against more targeted pitching or owned/social channels.
